page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.large is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with a dedicated Intel Xeon 6455B processor running at a high clock speed of 3.9 GHz. This configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2214.0 and strong single-threaded compression and decompression throughput, such as 34.49 GB/sec in gzip compression. However, due to its low core count of 1 physical core, multi-core performance is limited, as evidenced by a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 2683.0 and a poor stress-ng multi-core CPU performance rating. Memory bandwidth also shows constraints, with uncached large-block read bandwidth at 18.56 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 17.12 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7iz.large offers a high-frequency CPU and DDR5 memory allocation per core, making it a specialized entry point for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is well-suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight database operations, caching layers, and basic text or prompt processing tasks. It is less suitable for highly parallelized tasks, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or high-throughput web serving due to its limited multi-core capacity and baseline network speed.
